segments.zh: 欢迎回来，各位英语学习者。

segments.en: My name is Marco and I'm joined here by the lovely...
segments.zh: 我的名字是马可，可爱的人在这里加入了我的行列。

segments.en: And today we're going to be bringing you another great lesson, one of the lessons that you requested.
segments.zh: 今天，我们将为您带来另一个重要的课程，即您要求的课程之一。

segments.en: Actually, Maxim, Maxim S requested this one.
segments.zh: 实际上，Maxim，Maxim S 要求了这一点。

segments.en: I think he's really into research and investigation.
segments.zh: 我认为他真的是研究和调查。

segments.en: So we're bringing you a great lesson about this topic.
segments.zh: 因此，我们为您带来了有关该主题的精彩课程。

segments.en: So I'm really excited to hear this dialogue all about research.
segments.zh: 所以我很高兴听到这个关于研究的对话。

segments.en: So why don't we start listening to two university professors discussing an important question.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不开始听两位大学教授讨论一个重要问题。

segments.en: We've been over this a thousand times.
segments.zh: 这事我们已经讨论过无数次了。

segments.en: Look, we've done extensive research, built studies and read the literature, and there is conclusive evidence to support my theory.
segments.zh: 听着，我们做了大量研究、开展实验、查阅文献，已有确凿证据支持我的理论。

segments.en: Even in your most recent study, the investigative approach was flawed.
segments.zh: 就连你最近那项研究，方法也有问题。

segments.en: You know as well as I do, the collection of data was not systematic and there's a large margin of error.
segments.zh: 你我都清楚，数据收集不够系统，而且误差很大。

segments.en: To draw a definitive conclusion based on that data would be misleading.
segments.zh: 凭这些数据得出定论，会误导人。

segments.en: You are trying to single handedly solve one of the world's greatest mysteries and yet you're oblivious to the fact that you're wrong.
segments.zh: 你想单枪匹马解开世界上最大的谜团之一，却连自己错了都没意识到。

segments.en: Which came first, the chicken or the egg?
It's an age old question, isn't it?
segments.zh: 这是一个古老的问题，不是吗？

segments.en: And apparently they are not going to agree anytime soon.
segments.zh: 显然他们不会很快达成一致。

segments.en: All right, well, what they can agree about is this awesome language.
segments.zh: 好吧，好吧，他们能同意的是这种很棒的语言。

segments.en: So why don't we take a look at it now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不现在在语言外卖中看看它。

segments.en: Okay on Language Takeaway today we have some really great words and this first one is really good.
segments.zh: 好的，今天的语言外卖我们有一些非常棒的词，第一个真的很好。

segments.en: Okay so if the professor says that the data is irrefutable, what does he mean by that?
segments.zh: 好吧，如果教授说数据是无可辩驳的，他是什么意思？

segments.en: He's saying that you cannot deny it.
There is no way this is a lie.

segments.zh: 以无可辩驳的证据为例。
是的，这是一个很棒的短语。

segments.en: All right, so the professor complained that Dr. Horowitz's experiment was flawed.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以教授抱怨霍洛维茨博士的实验有缺陷。

segments.en: So flawed, is that an adjective, a verb or a noun?
segments.zh: 如此有缺陷，那是形容词、动词还是名词？

segments.en: Now when something is flawed, there is a problem with it, right?
segments.zh: 现在当有缺陷时，它有问题，对吧？

segments.en: Okay, so it has an error.
segments.zh: 好的，所以它有一个错误。

segments.en: So the professor is saying that his experiment has a flaw.
segments.zh: 所以教授说他的实验有缺陷。

segments.en: So flawed is the adjective of a flaw.
segments.zh: 所以有缺陷是缺陷的形容词。

segments.en: Now the reason that his study or his experiment was flawed is because it was not systematic.
segments.zh: 现在他的研究或实验有缺陷的原因是因为它不是系统的。

segments.en: So systematic, that's an interesting word.
segments.zh: 如此系统，这是一个有趣的词。

segments.en: Now I think we can recognize the word system in here, right?
segments.zh: 现在我想我们可以在这里识别系统这个词，对吧？

segments.en: So when something is systematic, it follows a process.
segments.zh: 因此，当某事是系统的时，它会遵循一个过程。

segments.en: So that's basically what systematic means, to follow a certain order, to be more organized, right?
segments.zh: 所以这基本上就是系统的意思，遵循一定的顺序，更有条理，对吧？

segments.en: And what about our next word?
segments.zh: 那么我们的下一个词呢？

segments.en: Okay, so what does it mean when I say that?
segments.zh: 好的，那我这么说是什么意思？

segments.en: I can't believe you said that.
Well, this is a really interesting phrase, but I think it's a little bit more common when it's used by older people.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是一个非常有趣的短语，但我认为当它被老年人使用时，它会更常见一点。

segments.en: I don't think, I don't really see a young person going up to someone and say, hey, that's preposterous.
segments.zh: 我不认为，我真的没有看到一个年轻人走到某人面前说，嘿，这很荒谬。

segments.en: Yeah, but it is a wonderful phrase.
segments.zh: 是的，但这是一个很棒的短语。

segments.en: Now our final phrase for takeaway, oblivious.
segments.zh: 现在是我们的最后一句话，忘记了。

segments.en: So a person that is oblivious to something.
segments.zh: 所以一个对某事视而不见的人。

segments.en: They don't know or they're unaware.
segments.zh: 他们不知道或他们不知道。

segments.en: Okay, so they ignore maybe the facts or they don't see it.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以他们可能忽略了事实，或者他们没有看到它。

segments.en: You're oblivious to the fact that we're in a recession.
segments.zh: 你忽略了我们正处于衰退中的事实。

segments.en: Okay, or he is completely oblivious.
segments.zh: 好吧，或者他完全忘记了。

segments.en: You can just say it like that, right?
Okay, so we took a look at some of the great vocabulary we found in the dialogue, but there were also some really good phrases that I think we should look at.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们看了一下我们在对话中发现的一些很棒的词汇，但也有一些非常好的短语，我认为我们应该看看。

segments.en: Okay, and let's take a look at those in Putting It Together.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们来看看那些把它放在一起的东西。

segments.en: You know, Marco, one of the things I love about English is the way that words seem to fit together, like blocks coming together.
segments.zh: 你知道，Marco，我喜欢英语的一件事是单词似乎融合在一起的方式，就像积木拼凑在一起。

segments.en: And here we have a lot of great examples of these words that fit together really nicely.
segments.zh: 在这里，我们有很多这些词的好例子，它们非常适合组合。

segments.en: Okay, so why don't we look at those?
segments.zh: 好吧，我们为什么不看看那些呢？

segments.en: And our first one now is extensive research.
segments.zh: 我们现在的第一个是广泛的研究。

segments.en: All right, so we know extensive means?
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们知道广泛的手段？

segments.en: So that's really good when you put it together, extensive research.
segments.zh: 所以当你把它放在一起时，这真的很好，广泛的研究。

segments.en: You have really studied, you have really looked things up.
segments.zh: 你真的学习了，你真的把事情看了。

segments.en: Another great research-related phrase here is conclusive evidence.
segments.zh: 这里另一个与研究相关的伟大短语是确凿的证据。

segments.en: All right, now, the first word there, conclusive.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在，那里的第一个词，结论性的。

segments.en: When something is conclusive, you can't argue with it.
segments.zh: 当某件事是决定性的时，你不能与它争论。

segments.en: All right, well, the professor complained that Horowitz's investigative approach was flawed, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，教授抱怨霍洛维茨的调查方法有缺陷，对吧？

segments.en: So this is our next phrase, investigative approach.
segments.zh: 所以这是我们的下一个短语，调查方法。

segments.en: Okay, so I remember the word investigate is a verb.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我记得调查这个词是一个动词。

segments.en: But in this case, it's a?
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，它是一个？

segments.en: So when something is investigative, it's obviously having to do with?
segments.zh: 那么，当某事进行调查时，它显然与之有关？

segments.en: So when he said investigative approach.
segments.zh: 所以当他说调查方法时。

segments.en: I mean, just simply the way you investigate the problem.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，只是你调查问题的方式。

segments.en: What about this other phrase that I saw?
segments.zh: 我看到的另一个短语呢？

segments.en: All right, well, again, I think we know the word conclusion, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，好吧，我想我们知道结论这个词，对吧？

segments.en: So it's a final judgment or decision.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个最终的判断或决定。

segments.en: When something is definitive, you can't argue with it or change it.
segments.zh: 当某件事是确定性的时，你不能与它争论或改变它。

segments.en: Okay, so the conclusion or the final result is final, like there is no way of arguing it.
segments.zh: 好的，所以结论或最终结果是最终的，就像没有办法争论它一样。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to it one more time in the dialogue?
segments.zh: 那么，我们为什么不在对话中再听一次呢？

segments.en: We've been over this a thousand times.
segments.zh: 这事我们已经讨论过无数次了。

segments.en: Look, we've done extensive research, built studies and read the literature, and there is conclusive evidence to support my theory.
segments.zh: 听着，我们做了大量研究、开展实验、查阅文献，已有确凿证据支持我的理论。

segments.en: Even in your most recent study, the investigative approach was flawed.
segments.zh: 就连你最近那项研究，方法也有问题。

segments.en: You know as well as I do, the collection of data was not systematic and there's a large margin of error.
segments.zh: 你我都清楚，数据收集不够系统，而且误差很大。

segments.en: To draw a definitive conclusion based on that data would be misleading.
segments.zh: 凭这些数据得出定论，会误导人。

segments.en: You are trying to single-handedly solve one of the world's greatest mysteries, and yet you're oblivious to the fact that you're wrong.
segments.zh: 你正试图单枪匹马地解决世界上最伟大的谜团之一，但你却忘记了自己错了的事实。

segments.en: What came first, the chicken or the egg?
segments.zh: 什么是先来的，鸡蛋还是鸡蛋？

segments.en: Well, you ask me, it was the egg.
What about why did the chicken cross the road?
To get to the other side.
Do you think that's really the reason?
segments.zh: 你认为这真的是原因吗？

segments.en: Well, there's a million different reasons, but this is great.
segments.zh: 嗯，有一百万种不同的原因，但这很棒。

segments.en: I'm glad you brought that up because this is like the classic English joke.
segments.zh: 我很高兴你提出了这个问题，因为这就像经典的英语笑话。

segments.en: Why did the chicken cross the road?
Well, there are a million answers.
So do you guys know any chicken jokes?
segments.zh: 那么你们知道有鸡笑话吗？

segments.en: Why don't you come to our website, EnglishPod.com, and on the comment section, why don't you leave us your thoughts on what came first, the chicken or the egg, and why do you think the chicken crossed the road?
segments.zh: 你为什么不来我们的网站 englishpod.com 和评论部分，你为什么不把你的想法留给我们先来，鸡还是鸡蛋，你为什么认为鸡肉过马路？

segments.en: Well, we really look forward to hearing your ideas, and Marco and I will be around to answer your questions.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们真的很期待听到您的想法，Marco 和我将随时回答您的问题。

segments.en: So I think we're out of time for today, but thanks for listening, and...
segments.zh: 所以我认为我们今天没有时间了，但感谢您的收听，并且...
